newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Crude Outlook - MidEast grades under pressure.
newsitem.headline: Asia Crude Outlook - MidEast grades under pressure.

text.p: Middle East crudes, trading in Asia, were expected to come under pressure this week amid weakening refinery margins.
Monthly buying tenders from India and Thailand's Bangchak Petroleum Plc could provide some support but the main focus would be on margins, traders said.
Shell Singapore said last week it has cut runs by around 30,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) at its 435,000-bpd refinery.
Esso Singapore confirmed earlier Monday it had instigated a 20 to 25-percent cut in runs for an indefinite period at its 230,000 bpd refinery.
Traders said other refiners in the region were considering similar cuts amid sharply lower middle distillate and fuel oil prices, which would not auger well for crude prices.

Indian Oil Corp (IOC) issued late last week its March buying tender. The tender closes January 30 and is valid for one day. However, traders said the tender would not significantly affect trading until next week.
Thailand's Bangchak Petroleum Plc was expected to issue its March tender later Monday to close later this week.
Bangchak has traditionally taken Oman crude as its major feedstock, but tight availability of Oman in its past two tenders prompted it to take Iranian heavy crude instead.
More Oman would be available for Bangchak this week, traders said.
March Oman crude traded last week at MPM +26 cents per barrel, after achieving premiums above +30 cents in the February market.
Traders said +26 was still a strong price considering Oman's differential to Dubai widened 18 cents in March from February.
By the end of the week traders said players were looking to shave a cent off traded prices, unsettled by several VLCCs of competing West African grades, which are due to arrive in Asia in March.
"I would expect Oman to see a steady 25 to 30 cents premiums for March," said an Oman seller.
Other Middle East grades were also under pressure.
Murban was heard trading around ADNOC +35 cents, down from +80 in February.
Umm Shaif traded at ADNOC +35 and +37 cents, from more than +80 in February, and Qatar Marine at between +25 and +48, down from a month-earlier +60.
"Prices are still strong this month, but everyone is comparing them to January and February," one trader said.
But interest for the lighter grades was being limited by Japanese refiners moving into more medium sweet grades for March having built up sufficient middle distillate stocks during the winter.
"Japanese throughput is coming down and in general the margins have been killed. No one is in a hurry to buy," one trader said.
However, there is relative support for Indonesian grades, which are trading February dates, from Japan, South Korea and China.
Benchmark Minas has traded as high as ICP +$1.20, up from near +90 cents in January. Higher prices up to +$1.30 have been achieved, but with conditions set on loading dates.
Regional light sweet grades were supported by tight availability for February.
Tapis producer Petronas is tentatively marketing March barrels at a premium of $1.85 after bringing March barrels forward into February and previously January into February.
Offers into Bangchak will provide the next indication of market sentiment over Tapis. The last February deal was concluded at +$1.75.
--Singapore Newsroom (+65 870 3081)
